title: Water Inlet Fault
shortDescription: Water did not enter the dishwasher within the allowed time.
fullDescription:
E1 indicates the Hisense dishwasher did not detect proper water fill. This can be a closed supply valve, clogged inlet screen, or failed inlet valve.

Start with water supply checks before replacing parts.

fixSteps.title: Clean inlet screen
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect supply hose and clean screen filter.

fixSteps.title: Replace valve
fixSteps.instruction: Swap in new inlet valve if needed.

whenToCallPro: If water connection requires plumbing modifications.

faq.a: Verify the supply valve is fully open.

title: Heating Fault
shortDescription: Water did not reach target temperature in time.
fullDescription:
E3 indicates the wash water failed to heat to setpoint within the allowed time. Possible causes: failed heating element, bad thermistor, or dry heater.

Washing continues without heat; dishes may not sanitize.
symptoms: Cold water at end of cycle

fixSteps.title: Test heater
fixSteps.instruction: Check continuity on the heating element.

whenToCallPro: If dishwasher must be pulled for access and you lack plumbing tools.

title: Overfill Fault
shortDescription: Too much water detected in the tub.
fullDescription:
E4 triggers when the float switch or level sensor sees water above normal. The drain pump runs to protect the dishwasher from leaks.

Stuck inlet valve or float is usually the cause.

fixSteps.title: Replace inlet valve
fixSteps.instruction: Swap inlet valve if stuck open.

faq.a: The anti-flood drain pump protects most leaks.

title: Turbidity Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The soil sensor has failed or is dirty.
fullDescription:
E5 indicates the turbidity (soil) sensor is not responding. The dishwasher defaults to a preset cycle length.

Often a cleaning restores function; otherwise replace the sensor assembly.

fixSteps.title: Clean sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Run a cleaner cycle and wipe sump area.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: If E5 persists, install new turbidity sensor.

whenToCallPro: If you can't access the sump without pulling the dishwasher.

title: Drain Fault
shortDescription: The dishwasher is not draining properly.
fullDescription:
H1 indicates water level did not drop within expected time. Usually a blocked filter, drain hose kink, or blocked disposer knockout.

Start with easy checks before replacing the drain pump.

fixSteps.title: Clean filter
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and wash the tub filter under running water.

fixSteps.title: Straighten hose
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure drain hose has a proper high loop with no kinks.

fixSteps.title: Test/replace drain pump
fixSteps.instruction: If still clogged, test drain pump and replace if failed.

whenToCallPro: If access requires pulling dishwasher from cabinet.

faq.a: If just installed, confirm the drain knockout plug was removed.

title: Heater Circuit Open
shortDescription: Heater circuit appears open at power-up test.
fullDescription:
H3 is a startup check failure on the heater circuit. The main control saw no current through the heater when commanded on.

Usually means a failed heating element or open thermal fuse.

fixSteps.title: Test heater
fixSteps.instruction: Ohm out the heater element for continuity.

fixSteps.title: Replace parts
fixSteps.instruction: Install new heater or thermal fuse.

faq.a: No - H3 blocks the cycle entirely.

title: Leak Detected
shortDescription: Water detected in the base pan.
fullDescription:
LE indicates the base-pan leak sensor (flood switch) has triggered. The dishwasher stops water flow and drains the tub.

Inspect for hose leaks, pump seal leaks, or a cracked tub.

fixSteps.title: Inspect base
fixSteps.instruction: Pull unit out and inspect base pan for water source.

fixSteps.title: Repair leak
fixSteps.instruction: Tighten clamp or replace leaking component.

whenToCallPro: If leak source is not obvious.

faq.a: Anti-flood systems drain the water to minimize damage.

title: Air Gap / Drain Air Trap Blocked
shortDescription: Drain air gap or air trap is blocked.
fullDescription:
AE indicates flow restriction at the drain air gap. If you have a countertop air gap, it may be clogged with debris.

Clean the air gap and confirm drain line.

fixSteps.title: Clean air gap
fixSteps.instruction: Remove cover and clean debris from air gap housing.

videoSearchQuery: Hisense dishwasher AE air gap clean

faq.a: Usually a small cylinder on the kitchen sink deck.

title: Thermistor Short
fullDescription:
F1 indicates the water temperature sensor is reading a short circuit. Heating is disabled for safety.

Replace the thermistor; check the harness for pinched wires.

fixSteps.title: Access sump
fixSteps.instruction: Remove tub filter and spray arm for access.

faq.a: F1 is a sensor short; H3 is a heater circuit open.

title: Thermistor Open
fullDescription:
F3 indicates the temperature sensor is open, so the control cannot read water temperature. Opposite fault from F1 but same resolution.

Replace the thermistor.

fixSteps.title: Check harness
fixSteps.instruction: Reseat thermistor connector on main PCB.

fixSteps.title: Replace thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new sensor if harness is good.

whenToCallPro: If sensor replacement doesn't clear code.
